title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index (April 2027), 10:00 a.m. ET
source: EST: the publisher's standing rule, restated on conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 332,019 bytes after one 301) — "The Conference Board publishes the Consumer Confidence Index (R) at 10 a.m. ET on the last Tuesday of every month." 2027-04-27 is the last Tuesday of April 2027. The rule is corroborated for APRIL specifically by three of the publisher's own dated next-release lines, each read off a March edition fetched direct 2026-09-06 at HTTP 200 and verified against its own "Source: March <year> Consumer Confidence Survey" line and "Updated:" date: CCI-Mar-2023 "The next release is Tuesday, April 25 at 10 AM ET", CCI-Mar-2024 "Tuesday, April 30th", CCI-Mar-2025 "Tuesday, April 29th" — each of which is the last Tuesday of its April. No April-2027 announcement exists yet, so this is the publisher's rule applied forward against a verified April record rather than a posted date. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: DISCOVERED during the consumer-confidence-2027-03-30 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06), one edition forward on the same chain by which 02-23 proposed 03-30. Proposed for two measured reasons, not bookkeeping. FIRST, it is the COLLISION COUNTERPART to its proposer. Per the Fed's own posted 2027 calendar (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, fetched 2026-09-06 HTTP 200, 164,831 bytes: Jan 26-27, Mar 16-17, Apr 27-28, Jun 8-9, Jul 27-28, Sep 14-15, Oct 26-27, Dec 7-8), 2027-04-27 IS FOMC DAY ONE -- one of exactly four colliding 2027 prints (01-26, 04-27, 07-27, 10-26) against eight clean ones. The 02-23 sibling registered FT-consumer-confidence-2027-02-23-2 to re-run its clean-vs-collision split after 2027-06-30, and this is the only 2027 collision instance inside that window other than 01-26. SECOND, and specific to this proposer, it is the natural REPLICATION SITE for the position-in-month control this ledger had to invent. The 03-30 research measured that March's width is FRONT-LOADED -- the last five March sessions run narrower than earlier March sessions on 6 of 9 instruments (SPY 1.019/1.353 p=0.0040, VIX 19.505/22.965 p=0.0012) -- so a last-Tuesday release compared against its own month reads as a spurious 3-of-9 narrowing that vanishes (0 of 9) against other late-month sessions. Whether that is a March artifact or a general property of the calendar month needs a month with a DIFFERENT within-month width profile, and April is the adjacent one. Note for whichever lane takes it: cut-off lags on the sourced March editions run 8/8/6 days, which would put an April-2027 panel at roughly 04-01 -> 04-20, entirely inside the intermeeting window and closing before fomc-blackout-start-2027-04-17 has run its course -- so unlike 03-30, this edition prints INSIDE the blackout, on decision-eve, and its release-day tape cannot be attributed to the survey at all. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
